transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep jumping into big plans and trips without thinking, and it’s starting to cause problems for my family. They got really worried when I suddenly took off on a long drive to visit an old coworker without telling anyone, so they insisted I come in to talk to someone.
Have you ever had similar periods before where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, and became more impulsive or talkative for several days at a time?

No, I don't recall ever having an episode like this before in my life. This level of intense energy and making all these sudden plans feels entirely new to me. It really only started about a month ago, right after I got the news about my firm retirement date.

Have you ever had any previous episodes like this in the past, even if they were milder or shorter, where you had unusually high energy, needed much less sleep, or became more impulsive or talkative for several days?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before now. I have always been known as a warm, steady person until this past month when all this started. This is completely new territory for me and my family.

Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable for several days and it caused problems, even if it happened years ago? This helps us tell whether this is a first episode or part of a bipolar pattern.

No, I really don't recall ever having a period like this in my past. Everyone has always known me as a very warm, steady person until this recent month. This is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this.
How long has this period of unusually high energy, reduced need for sleep, and impulsive behavior been going on continuously? Has it lasted at least one week?

Yes, it has definitely been going on much longer than one week. This high energy and impulsive behavior has been continuous for about a month now, ever since my supervisor pushed me to set a firm retirement date.
During this time, have you had any experiences like hearing voices, seeing things others could not, or feeling that people are trying to harm or control you?

No, nothing like that at all—I haven't heard or seen anything unusual, and I don't feel like anyone is trying to harm me. My main issue is just that I have way too much energy, my mind is constantly racing, and I can't stop making all these big plans.

During this time, have you felt so energized or confident that you were able to do much more than usual, or has it caused serious problems like needing hospitalization or making it impossible to function at work or at home?

Yes, I've been feeling incredibly energized and trying to do way more than usual, like rearranging my workshop and double-booking myself with endless church projects. While I haven't been hospitalized, it has caused serious problems; I've missed mentoring commitments, upset church leaders, and my wife says she can no longer rely on me or feel safe with what I might do next.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a first lifetime episode of elevated/expansive mood with markedly increased energy, racing thoughts, impulsive grand plans, reduced sleep need implied by sustained high energy, and clear functional disruption lasting about one month. There are no psychotic symptoms, and the episode has not required hospitalization, supporting manic episode without psychotic symptoms rather than manic episode with psychosis.
